name: Old pink
lede: Old pink is a moderate, dusty pink carried in Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955, measured in our color graph as identical to a separately sourced name, Corinthian Pink.

sections.title: The same pink, twice over
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* records this hue, and the ISCC-NBS system later filed it as a moderate pink, both cited in our library alongside Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary [1]. Our color graph finds a separately recorded name, Corinthian Pink, at zero units of difference, an exact duplicate under a different name [2]. The library also lists eight further alternate names on nearby chips, among them Tuscany, Light Purplish Vinaceous and Mauve Mist, though only some resolve to colors in our data [2].

Its nearest distinct relatives in the color graph are [[tuscany]], almost the same, and [[pastel-pink]] and [[rosy-brown]], both a little further off [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Old pink covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 76 works, rarer than 52 per cent of our named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 6 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.8 times the archive's overall rate, and is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 3.9 times expected [4]. The earliest dated appearance in our archive is the year 1000, nine centuries before the name's own 1912 record, a look-alike hue, not proof of pigment or dye, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [4].
